sources.title: Structured interview note preserving recursive/non-recursive inorder prompt

claims.text: The source requires both recursive and non-recursive binary-tree inorder traversal, while node API, return shape, empty-tree behavior and language are not source-frozen.

Under the declared Java TreeNode/List contract, both candidate traversals match an independent Morris inorder oracle over fixed, skewed and random trees, preserve the tree, and the iterative form handles a 50,000-node skew boundary.

validation.command: independent Morris traversal oracle and deep iterative boundary

boundary_tests.case: null, single, balanced, left-skew and right-skew trees
boundary_tests.expected: recursive and iterative traversals equal independent Morris inorder oracle

boundary_tests.case: 30,000 seeded random trees with duplicate values
boundary_tests.expected: both candidate methods equal Morris oracle and preserve tree structure
temporary threads are fully removed and original tree shape is restored
iterative traversal completes with ordered full output without relying on JVM recursion depth

findings: The frozen source explicitly requires binary-tree inorder traversal in both recursive and non-recursive forms; node representation, return type, empty-tree result and implementation language are not preserved source constraints.
The candidate declares those missing details as a Java reference contract instead of presenting them as source facts, and it supplies both required implementations.
The recursive left-root-right implementation and the explicit left-chain stack implementation satisfy the same inorder ordering invariant.

An independent Morris-traversal oracle, structurally different from both candidate implementations and the writer fixture, matches both methods across fixed/skewed cases and 30,000 seeded random trees with duplicate values; temporary Morris threads are verified to restore the original tree.

Time O(n), auxiliary O(h) for recursion/explicit stack, deep-recursion risk, no-mutation behavior, Morris O(1) tradeoff, and the no-fabricated-project-experience boundary are explicit and consistent with the executable evidence.
